name: The Engraved Ring
summary: High Executor Hadrec sends an adventurer to Brill carrying a recovered wedding band inscribed to a woman named Deliah. Magistrate Sevren consults town records to identify her origins, seeking clues about her life and the person who gave her the ring.

sections.title: A Keepsake in Silverpine
sections.body: While investigating the Rot Hide gnolls infesting the northern edges of Silverpine Forest, scouts uncovered an engraved ring bearing the name Deliah. Rather than discard the trinket, High Executor Hadrec directs you to take it back across the border to Brill. As Magistrate Sevren maintains the civic records and burial registers of the Tirisfal region, he is the most likely official to identify who she was—even if Hadrec remains deeply cynical about whether anyone among the Forsaken still cares.

sections.title: Stolen from the Soil
sections.body: Upon receiving the ring in Brill, Magistrate Sevren confirms that Deliah was indeed a resident who died and was interred within the town's mass grave. Finding her jewelry among the Rot Hides in Silverpine reveals a sinister desecration: the plague-warped gnolls have been raiding mass graves and spiriting corpses southward for Scourge experiments, leaving Sevren eager to see the gnolls wiped out.

faq.answer: Deliah is the name engraved on the recovered ring. Hadrec asks you to consult Magistrate Sevren's records in Brill to learn who she was.

faq.q: Why was Deliah's ring found in Silverpine Forest?
aliases: why do gnolls have the ring
how did ring get to silverpine
faq.answer: The ring was recovered during the Rot Hide investigation. Sevren's records may help explain whose keepsake it was and how it came to Silverpine.

faq.q: Why does High Executor Hadrec doubt the ring matters?
faq.answer: Hadrec notes that undeath often strips away mortal attachments. He assumes Deliah's lover is either dead or, if risen as Forsaken, entirely indifferent to mortal vows and memories.

faq.q: What role does Magistrate Sevren play in this quest?
faq.answer: As the magistrate of Brill, Sevren maintains the local municipal records and registers of the dead, allowing him to confirm Deliah's identity and burial site.

faq.q: Are the Rot Hide gnolls allied with the Scourge?
faq.answer: Yes. The Rot Hide gnolls of Silverpine Forest were infected by the Scourge plague, operating under dark influences and collecting corpses for necromantic purposes.

faq.q: Where does this investigation lead next?
faq.answer: Magistrate Sevren consults Brill's records to identify Deliah. What he learns provides the next lead in the investigation.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, Deliah's ring is a quiet reminder of the fragile threads connecting their living pasts to their grim, cold present in Lordaeron.
Stopping the Rot Hide gnolls from desecrating Horde-controlled graves in Tirisfal is a matter of territorial security as much as retribution.
